newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian bourse to release short-selling list.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian bourse to release short-selling list.

text.p: A list of 20 to 30 approved stocks permitted to be traded under regulated short-selling will be released on September 27, the national Bernama news agency reported on Wednesday.

Bernama quoted Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) market development senior manager S. Loganathan, who said, "The list will be reviewed every six months and there could be further addition or reduction to the number of approved securities."
Regulated short-selling will start on September 30. The practice refers to selling securities that one does not own in the hopes of replacing the shares when the price is lower.

The criteria for approved securities include an average daily market capitalisation of over 2 billion ringgit for the past three months, at least 100 million shares in public float and a minimum of 2,000 registered shareholders.
The firms must also have five years' uninterrupted after-tax profit record and an average monthly share volume traded of more than two million shares for the past 12 calendar months.
"As of last year, we have 28 such eligible shares," Loganathan said, adding that there must be enough liquidity in the stocks before short-sale could be permitted.
